shape: Canadian mortgage lead-gen marketplace — pre-reputation brand in a trust-critical regulated category; tests the binder away from India, on a LEAD conversion event and an intangible financial service, and as a fresh mid-fame brand to probe whether the sourcing/no-fabrication failures seen on TWT track brand-fame (recall temptation) or are general binder gaps
notes: Third research fixture, added S111 (2026-05-22) as a generalization + overfitting check after TWT was run 5×. Deliberate contrasts to both existing fixtures: (1) NON-India locale — Canada, English; the binder must not assume Indian context (CPM/CPL ranges, festivals, Tenglish register all inapplicable); verify cost-reality and calendar adapt to a Canadian frame. (2) LEAD conversion event (mortgage lead form), not a purchase (TWT) or a site-visit/enquiry (arjun-infra). (3) Intangible regulated financial service, not a physical product — §4 visual reality should handle the no-tangible-product, no-reference-images case honestly. (4) MID-FAME brand — far less training-data presence than TWT; THIS IS THE KEY TEST: TWT failed sourced + no-fabrication because Haiku recalled famous-brand specifics (hex codes, competitor revenues) from training and dressed them as research. TheRateFinder has little to recall, so if those criteria PASS here, the TWT failures were brand-fame artifacts (binder generalizes, don't patch it); if they FAIL here too, the gap is general and the binder needs the recall-guard edit. (5) Expected real-world findings the apprentice should DISCOVER (not given in intake): it is a lead-gen marketplace not a consumer rate tool; thin-to-zero third-party reviews; legitimacy signals (licence, named brokers) may be absent; possible stale published rates; the name promises the most commoditized lane while the product may run deeper. The apprentice should surface what it can source and name the rest as gaps — NOT fabricate the legitimacy/rate specifics. (6) Apprentice model is Haiku 4.5 for this run (production target); judge is Sonnet 4.6.
